chapterName: Middle Republic: Rome Turns East (200-167 BCE)

questions.question: A talent, the unit used for Philip V's war payment to Rome, was roughly how much silver?
questions.explanation: A talent was roughly 26 kg of silver. Philip had to pay 1,000 of them after his defeat.
questions.sourceQuote: Philip had to withdraw every garrison from the Greek cities of Europe and Asia and pay 1,000 talents, a talent being roughly 26 kg of silver.

questions.question: What title did Antiochus III earn after recovering Armenia and Iran and taking Syria and Judea?
questions.explanation: His sweeping conquests won Antiochus III the title "Great King". With Philip beaten, he pushed into western Asia Minor and then crossed into Thrace.
questions.sourceQuote: He had brought Armenia and Iran back under his control and taken Syria and Judea from Egypt, earning the title "Great King".

questions.question: Why were Roman soldiers not frightened by the lunar eclipse the night before Pydna?
options: Priests declared it a lucky sign
They had seen one at Cynoscephalae
questions.explanation: Because an officer had predicted the eclipse, the Roman troops stayed calm. Aemilius still offered sacrifice after sacrifice until the omens were favourable.
questions.sourceQuote: An officer had predicted it, so the Roman soldiers were not frightened.

questions.question: What does the name Cynoscephalae, the hills where Rome fought Philip V in 197 BC, mean?
questions.explanation: Cynoscephalae means "Dog's Heads". The hills lie in Thessaly, where the two armies were camped near each other in June 197 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: In June 197 BC the two armies were camped near each other among the Cynoscephalae hills, whose name means "Dog's Heads", in Thessaly.

questions.question: How did Flamininus defeat Philip V at the Aous river gorge?
options: He blocked the gorge and starved the Macedonians out
He lured Philip onto open ground with a pretended retreat
He sent troops along a hidden mountain path to attack from behind
He landed troops by sea behind the Macedonian camp
questions.explanation: The ground favoured the Macedonians, but Flamininus was shown a hidden path through the mountains. Philip fled into Thessaly, leaving about 2,000 men dead or wounded.
questions.sourceQuote: He sent troops round to strike from behind, and Philip fled into Thessaly, leaving about 2,000 men dead or wounded.

questions.question: Which Roman consul was sent in 168 BC to finish the war against Perseus?
questions.explanation: Aemilius Paullus, an experienced consul serving for the second time, was sent to end the war. He went on to win at Pydna and celebrate a triumph.
questions.sourceQuote: In 168 BC Rome sent Aemilius Paullus, an experienced consul serving for the second time, to finish the war against Perseus, king of Macedon.

questions.question: What did Flamininus proclaim at the Isthmian Games of 196 BC?
options: Freedom for the Greek communities Philip had ruled
A new war against Antiochus III
Roman annexation of Macedon as a province
questions.explanation: At the great festival near Corinth, Flamininus proclaimed freedom (libertas) for the Greeks, and the crowd erupted in joy. The freedom had limits, though: Roman troops stayed in key fortresses.
questions.sourceQuote: At the Isthmian Games of May 196 BC, a great festival near Corinth, the Roman commander Flamininus proclaimed freedom (*libertas*) for the Greek communities Philip had ruled.

questions.question: Who took command of Rome's war against Philip V in 198 BC?
questions.explanation: Flamininus took over in 198 BC while still under thirty. He hardened Rome's demands and soon beat Philip at the Aous river.
questions.sourceQuote: In 198 BC command passed to Flamininus, a consul not yet thirty who proudly called himself a lover of Greek culture.

questions.question: What was the Macedonian phalanx?
options: A flexible formation of small, independent units
A screen of light troops armed with javelins
A dense block of men armed with very long spears
A wedge of heavy cavalry led by the king
questions.explanation: The phalanx was a dense mass of spearmen with very long spears. At Cynoscephalae the more flexible Roman legions beat it.
questions.sourceQuote: Macedon relied on the phalanx, a dense block of men armed with very long spears.

questions.question: After the Peace of Apamea, who received the land Antiochus III gave up?
options: Rome, as its first eastern province
Egypt, which recovered its lost lands
questions.explanation: Rome took no land for itself and handed the territory to its loyal allies. The Aetolians, by contrast, were reduced to a dependent state.
questions.sourceQuote: The territory went to its loyal allies, Pergamon and Rhodes.
